setup: Face away from the stack, handle behind you
Step forward until the cable is taut
execution: Start with the arm long behind your hip
Curl the handle forward and up
Lower slowly back to the stretch
faults: Don't let your elbow swing forward
Don't twist your body to help
Don't let the cable snap your arm back

notes: The start stretches the front of the shoulder; ease into it with a light weight and control the return.
If the stretched position is uncomfortable, shorten it by standing closer to the stack.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Cable curl
regressions.reason: Facing the stack; less stretch at the shoulder.

progressions.name: Bayesian curl with a pause in the stretch
progressions.reason: A short hold at the bottom adds time under tension.

substitutions.name: Incline dumbbell curl
substitutions.reason: Also curls with the arm behind the body.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell curl
substitutions.reason: No cable needed; load is each dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Preacher curl
substitutions.reason: Arm in front of the body; a trial found similar growth to the Bayesian curl.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at chest height, cable column behind the figure on the left, working arm nearest the camera. The cable line from the low pulley to the hand must stay visible.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Standing a step or two in front of the column, facing away, staggered stance, slight forward lean. Near arm straight and drawn back behind the hip by the cable, palm forward.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Elbow bent and the handle curled up near the shoulder. Upper arm still angled slightly behind the body; it hasn't swung forward.

ikHints: Hand fixed to the handle; cable runs back to the low pulley
doNotShow: Arm yanked back by the cable

sources.title: Attarieh et al. 2025, Eur J Sport Sci 25(4): Preacher versus Bayesian cable curls
sources.supports: secondaryMuscles (brachialis); variations.substitutions[3] (15 young men, 10 weeks: no significant difference in biceps or brachialis growth, or strength, between the two curls)
sources.note: Abstract only, read through Europe PMC (PubMed needed cookies). Small within-subject study.

uncertain.note: The idea that training the biceps in a stretched position grows it more is popular, but the one trial checked found no difference against the preacher curl. No growth advantage is claimed.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. Negative shoulder flexion means the arm is behind the body.
